newsitem.title: USA: Charleston, S.C. $72.2 mln budget holds tax steady.
newsitem.headline: Charleston, S.C. $72.2 mln budget holds tax steady.

text.p: Charleston, S.C., Mayor Joseph Riley has proposed a $72.2 million budget that holds property taxes steady for 1997.
The budget Riley released on Tuesday would raise parking fees to $1.50 per hour from $1 per hour on city streets.

The budget reprsents a 4.6 percent increase over this year's $69 million budget, with most of the increase targeted for police. It includes a $4.3 million general obligation bond issue to finance the purchase of property on James Island and to build fire stations on James and John's Islands.

The mayor said he would also seek a second 1997 bond issue to finance repairs at the city's Market Hall issue. Debt service for the unspecified issue would be paid with revenues from the city's new accommodations tax.
The City Council must approve a 1997 budget by Jan 1.
